title: The Number of Man as generation count
statement: Per the canon's third book, the number 666 of Revelation 13:18 is read not as a coded name but as a count: the number of human generations from the creation of the first finalized humans in the laboratories to the 1945 nuclear threshold — tying the Apocalypse's most notorious cipher to the era-opening of woh-claim-0031; the reading is canon-explicit, and its arithmetic dependence on the corpus's chronology is declared rather than hidden.

includes: The canonical reading: 666 as generation count from creation to the threshold, as the third book states it
The chronology coupling: the count's arithmetic runs against the age-lattice of woh-claim-0003 and the threshold of woh-claim-0031, and the record declares the dependence
The contrast the canon draws: the count reading against the name-cipher tradition (gematria on Nero and its successors), with the mainstream account preserved
excludes: Verification arithmetic in prose; generation-length assumptions vary and the corpus does not publish a computation as if it were the canon's
The name-cipher scholarship as target; the Nero gematria remains the mainstream account of the text's composition-era meaning
Extension to other apocalyptic numbers without records
Any eschatological date-setting, excluded here as in woh-claim-0015

source_references.locator: Revelation 13:18 (the number of the beast; 'it is the number of a man')

alternatives.statement: The number is Neron Caesar in gematria, the composition-era reading with manuscript support (the 616 variant); the count reading has no purchase on the text's own world.
Generation counts are elastic enough to hit any target; the reading's arithmetic is unfalsifiable as framed.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0003 or woh-claim-0031 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the reading.
Public prose begins publishing verification arithmetic or extending to other apocalyptic numbers, both of which this record excludes.
